new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Work 0, Oparemi 2011, sect. 2.2 'Tone system in Koenoem language', p. 72 per the table of contents (file, the passage beginning 'Koenoem is a tone language'): 'Koenoem is a tone language. It has three basic register tones. In Koenoem, tone is contrastive in that words that have the same orthographical representation are differentiated by the tone i.e. tonal differences bring about a change in the meaning of the affected words.' with L/M/H examples ([kàà] 'climb', [tágbó] 'lizard', [fuat] 'vomit', [bìsá] 'food', [làbárì] 'story'). sources.citation: Decker, Ken; Christina Riepe; Adedamola Aregbesola; Fittokka Gobak; John Sacson; Samuel Eju. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Koenoem [kcs] Language of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-021. Dallas: SIL International. 55 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 6.2 'Phonology' (printed p. 10-11) gives only 'initial, cursory observations' (consonant and vowel inventories, labialization/palatalization, vowel length); no mention of stress, accent or word-level tone. Appendix E (printed p. 34) states: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' The 348-item wordlist is untoned.
